description: A finance director must approve a supplier early-payment program and finalize its eligibility, concentration, tax, and contracting controls, with input from risk, accounts payable, tax, and legal.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed paying participating suppliers 30 days before invoice maturity in exchange for a 2% early-payment discount.
shared_context.S2: The proposal would initially allow all approved suppliers to participate, with no single-supplier cap or special tax reserve stated.
shared_context.S3: The program would be funded from the company's operating cash and would be reviewed each quarter.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding approval decision for the program.
shared_context.S5: As part of the finance approval routine, Elena asks risk, accounts payable, tax, and legal for their final desk updates before approving the operating terms.

PF1.text: Malik completed the program exposure review this morning and found that internal working-capital policy permits no more than $1,500,000 of eligible early-payment invoices from any one supplier; he recorded the result in his draft review, which has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Jenna confirmed while reconciling this week's invoice file that $2,200,000 of the largest supplier's invoices are under active commercial dispute and must not be enrolled in early payment; the dispute list has not yet been attached to the program proposal.

PF3.text: Ravi received a tax memorandum this morning stating that each cross-border supplier payment under this program requires a 1.25% withholding reserve and remittance within 10 calendar days; the memorandum has not yet been added to the tax checklist.

PF4.text: Claire found in the standard supplier agreement this week that participation requires a signed supplier opt-in and 15 business days' termination notice; she has not yet updated the draft program terms.

acceptance_conditions: The program must be approved with a single-supplier eligible-invoice cap of exactly $1,500,000.
Invoices under active commercial dispute must be excluded from early payment.
A 1.25% withholding reserve must be maintained for cross-border supplier payments.
Tax remittance for those payments must occur within 10 calendar days.
Supplier participation must require a signed opt-in and 15 business days' termination notice.

decisive_facts.why: The shared proposal has no concentration limit, while PF1 changes single_supplier_invoice_cap_usd from an unrestricted program to exactly 1500000 and supplies the policy basis that must be cited.
The shared proposal permits all approved invoices, while PF2 changes disputed_invoices_excluded from false or unspecified to true by removing the $2,200,000 of invoices under active dispute.
The shared proposal states no tax reserve or remittance timing, while PF3 changes withholding_reserve_percent to exactly 1.25 and tax_remittance_days to no more than 10.
The shared proposal has no supplier contracting controls, while PF4 changes supplier_termination_notice_business_days to exactly 15 and requires the signed_supplier_opt_in commitment.
